svg.aria-label: Inside a scheduler queue, wakeup, select and replay
svg.text: Inside a scheduler queue, wakeup, select and replay
A matrix scheduler fits what is measured, operands read at issue and queues that do not shift. The entry format and the replay rule are proposed.
integer queue of about 13; proposed on top of the patent
Pairing, the size dispute and the load shadow
Issue ports to the register file
rA, rB: ready bits, set by wakeup
shadow: 3 bit timer from the load that woke this uop
while the timer runs the entry stays after issue, to reissue +
operands are read from the register file at issue ●
entry 1 completes: column 1 clears, row 3 is ready
wakeup is a column clear, one wire per entry
select: the ready entry with no older ready entry
allocation writes one row and one column
the rest; fills gaps the primary leaves
Q1 with Q2, Q3 with Q4, Q5 with Q6
nothing ready: issue from the partner
one age matrix per pair would do it
Johnson: 24 per int queue, 28 per mul queue
Handley: each pair counted twice, so 13
drawn as 13; 134 is the hard number
Speculative wakeup behind a load, proposed from the patent
the consumer is woken for cycle 3 as if the load hits
a store address resolving late causes a replay, not a flush ○
the replaying load waits in a load execution queue ?
test: k dependent ALU ops behind a load that replays once
cost grows with k until k passes the shadow depth
14 units with up to 2 sources: 28 reads
4 banks means about 7 reads per bank, too many
proposed: bank by register number mod 4
a bank conflict stalls select by a cycle
int to SIMD: a fake load, about 6 cycles
SIMD to int: a dedicated path, about 6 cycles
MADD feeds the next addend in 1 cycle
int divide: a side pipe, one every 2 cycles
One possibly mispredicting op a cycle
short age bits say what to flush
ALU ops sourcing one bank, versus spread
